title: Rajasthan: Udaipur, Jodhpur, Jaisalmer, Pushkar and Ajmer, Ranthambore, Mount Abu, Chittorgarh, Kumbhalgarh and Bikaner
selection: Rajasthan is one of India's most visited states, but VacayOut had full content only for Jaipur; nine destinations existed as empty pages. This pack fills them, adds Ajmer, their main sights and things to do, and state-wide itineraries and guides — researched from Rajasthan Tourism (Government of Rajasthan), UNESCO and Wikipedia.

RJW1.claim: Winter, from about October to January, is the best time to visit Rajasthan, with temperatures of roughly 10–30°C in most parts.

evidence.quote: Winters  – The winters are marked as being the best season to visit Rajasthan.
the princely state enjoys a mild weather with temperatures ranging between 10°C – 30°C for most parts
Winters in Rajasthan usually commence around October and extend to January.

RJW2.claim: The Jaipur Literature Festival, Udaipur World Music Festival and Pushkar Fair all fall in the winter season.

evidence.quote: including the Jaipur Literature Festival, Udaipur World Music Festival, Camel Fair, and Pushkar Fair, are observed during the winter season

RJW3.claim: Summers are hot and dry, with temperatures up to 48°C; Mount Abu, Ranakpur and Kumbhalgarh are pleasant in summer.

evidence.quote: Summers in Rajasthan are usually hot and dry, with temperatures rising up to as high as 48 degrees Celsius.
summers in places like Mount Abu, Ranakpur, and Kumbhalgarh in Rajasthan, which are the places to which tourists mostly flock to when visiting the state in this season, are rather pleasant

RJW4.claim: In the monsoon, Rajasthan turns green and celebrates the Teej festival.

evidence.quote: Visiting Rajasthan during the monsoon season, you will be welcomed by lush greenery, rainbows, and peacocks dancing around.
as various parts of the state ready up for the Teej festival in the monsoon season

RJW5.claim: Rajasthan's three major airports are Jaipur (domestic and international), Jodhpur and Udaipur (domestic).

evidence.quote: The three major airports of Rajasthan are Sanganer International Airport in Jaipur, Jodhpur Airport and Dabok Airport in Udaipur.
While Sanganer is open to domestic and international air traffic, Jodhpur and Udaipur only serve domestic routes

RJW6.claim: Jaipur and Kota are the main rail hubs; Udaipur, Jodhpur, Ajmer, Bikaner and Abu Road are other major stations.

evidence.quote: The major railway stations of Rajasthan are Jaipur, Kota, Bharatpur, Bikaner, Ajmer, Alwar, Udaipur, Abu Road and Jodhpur.
But out of this lot, Jaipur and Kota are major hubs connecting the major cities of India to Rajasthan.

RJW7.claim: NH-8 between Delhi and Mumbai runs through Jaipur, Ajmer, Udaipur and Chittorgarh; RSRTC runs state buses.

evidence.quote: The NH-8 which connects Mumbai to Delhi is the busiest national highway in Rajasthan and runs through Ajmer, Jaipur, Udaipur and Chittorgarh.
hop onto a bus operated by the Rajasthan State Road Transport Corporation

RJW8.claim: The Hill Forts of Rajasthan — Chittorgarh, Kumbhalgarh, Ranthambore (Sawai Madhopur), Gagron (Jhalawar), Amber (Jaipur) and Jaisalmer — became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2013.

evidence.quote: The serial site, situated in the state of Rajastahan, includes six majestic forts in Chittorgarh; Kumbhalgarh; Sawai Madhopur; Jhalawar; Jaipur, and Jaisalmer.
They have been clustered as a series and designated as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2013.

UD1.claim: Udaipur, the 'Venice of the East', is a city of lakes ringed by the green Aravalli hills; the Lake Palace stands in the middle of Lake Pichola.

evidence.quote: Often referred to as the 'Venice of the East', the city of lakes Udaipur is located around azure water lakes and is hemmed in by lush green hills of Aravallis.
The famous Lake Palace, located in the middle of Lake Pichola is one of the most beautiful sights of Udaipur.

UD2.claim: Udaipur was founded in 1553 by Maharana Udai Singh II as the new capital of Mewar.

evidence.quote: Udaipur was founded in 1553 by Maharana Udai Singh II as the new capital of Mewar Kingdom.

UD3.claim: The ten-day Shilpgram arts and crafts festival runs from 21 to 30 December.

evidence.quote: The ten-day Shilpgram Festival which starts from 21 Dec to 30 Dec pulls in a large number of people interested in arts and crafts.

UD4.claim: Maharana Pratap Airport at Dabok is about 25 km north-east of the city centre.

evidence.quote: Dabok Airport, also known as Maharana Pratap Airport is the closest at about 25 km northeast of the city centre.

UD5.claim: Udaipur is linked by road and rail with Chittorgarh, Ajmer, Jaipur, Ahmedabad, Delhi and Mumbai.

evidence.quote: Udaipur is connected by rail to several major cities in India including Chittorgarh, Ahmedabad, Ajmer, Sawai Madhopur, Jaipur, Agra, Delhi, Mumbai and Khajuraho.

UD6.claim: The Mewar Festival welcomes spring in Udaipur.

evidence.quote: The festival is observed to welcome the arrival of spring.

UD7.claim: A ropeway from Deen Dayal Upadhyay Park climbs to the Karni Mata Temple, with views over the city.

evidence.quote: At the Deen Dayal Upadhyay Park, a special ropeway ride takes you to the top of the hill towards the Karni Mata Temple.

UD8.claim: Sajjangarh, the 19th-century Monsoon Palace on the Bansdara hills, gives sweeping views of the city.

evidence.quote: Situated just outside Udaipur, this 19th-century palace is built on top of Bansdara hills.
It is still an awe-inspiring sight on the Udaipur skyline and offers spectacular views of the city and the areas around.

UDC1.claim: The City Palace towers over Lake Pichola: a complex of courtyards, pavilions, terraces and hanging gardens entered through the triple-arched Tripolia gate.

evidence.quote: A majestic architectural marvel towering over the lake on a hill surrounded by crenelated walls, it is a conglomeration of courtyards, pavilions, terraces, corridors, rooms and hanging gardens.
The main entrance is through the triple arched gate, the "Tripolia" with eight marble porticos

UDC2.claim: Inside, the Mor Chowk is known for its glass peacock mosaics; a sound and light show runs every evening at Manak Chowk.

evidence.quote: The 'MorChowk' known for its exquisite peacock mosaics in glass and the 'ChiniChitrashala' noted for its blue and white ceramics are other attractions in the palace.
A high tech sound and light show is conducted every evening at the magnificent ManakChowk which brings alive the rich history of Mewar.

UDC3.claim: The palace's Crystal Gallery holds one of the largest collections of Osler cut glass, mostly commissioned by Maharana Sajjan Singh in 1878.

evidence.quote: The Udaipur Collection of crystal is one of the largest and most complete collections of Osler cut glass in existence.
Most of this collection was commissioned by Maharana Sajjan Singh in 1878

UDL1.claim: Lake Pichola holds the islands of Jagniwas and Jagmandir, with the City Palace on its eastern bank; a sunset boat ride gives the best views.

evidence.quote: The islands of Jagniwas and Jagmandir are housed in this lake.
Along the eastern banks of the lake lies the City Palace.
A boat ride in the lake around sunset offers a breathtaking view of the Lake and City Palace.

UDL2.claim: The Lake Palace (Jagniwas), built 1743–1746 as a summer palace, is now a hotel.

evidence.quote: Now a hotel but was originally called Jagniwas and served as a summer palace.
Built between 1743 and 1746 on the island near Jagmandir in Lake Pichola

UDJ1.claim: Jag Mandir, the island 'Lake Garden Palace' on Lake Pichola, was built between 1620 and about 1652 and once sheltered Prince Khurram, later Shah Jahan.

evidence.quote: Also called the ‘Lake Garden Palace’, the construction for this began in 1620 and was completed around 1652.
Interestingly, Prince Khurram - later Emperor Shah Jahan - was given shelter here when he rebelled against his father Emperor Jahangir.

UDT1.claim: The three-storey Jagdish Temple, dedicated to Vishnu, was built in 1651 by Maharana Jagat Singh I.

evidence.quote: An example of the Indo-Aryan style of architecture, Jagdish Temple was built in 1651 and continues to be one of the most famous temples in and around Udaipur.
This three-storied temple was built by Maharana Jagat Singh I.

UDS1.claim: Saheliyon-ki-Bari, a garden built by Maharana Sangram Singh II for women, has marble elephants, fountains, kiosks and a lotus pool.

evidence.quote: Built by Maharana Sangram Singh II as a garden for women, Saheliyon-ki-Bari or the Garden of the Maidens is a popular tourist destination.
Along with a small museum, it has several attractions such as marble elephants, fountains, kiosks and a lotus pool.

UDB1.claim: Bagore-ki-Haveli at Gangaur Ghat was built in the 18th century by Mewar's prime minister and has over a hundred rooms.

evidence.quote: Bagore-ki-Haveli is located by Lake Pichola, at Gangaur Ghat. Amar Chand Badwa, the Prime Minister of Mewar, built it in the 18th century.
The massive palace has over a hundred rooms that display costumes and modern art.

UDB2.claim: The Dharohar folk dance show is held in the evenings at Bagore-ki-Haveli's Neem Chowk.

evidence.quote: Bagore Dance Show (officially called Dharohar), at Neem Chowk, is a joyous melange of good ambience, music and performances.

UDF1.claim: Fateh Sagar lies north of Lake Pichola, linked by a canal, and holds Nehru Island and India's only island solar observatory.

evidence.quote: This delightful lake, bordered by hills and woodlands, lies to the north of Lake Pichola.
This artificial lake is connected to Lake Pichola by a canal.
Solar observatory in Lake Fateh Sagar is the only observatory in India located on an island

UDF2.claim: On Moti Magri above Fateh Sagar stands a bronze statue of Maharana Pratap on his horse Chetak.

evidence.quote: An impressive bronze statue of Maharana Pratap on his favourite horse Chetak, stands atop the Moti Magri overlooking Fateh Sagar.

JD1.claim: Jodhpur, Rajasthan's second-largest city, is known as the Blue City for its blue-painted buildings.

evidence.quote: Jodhpur, the second largest city in Rajasthan is popularly known as the Blue City.
The name is clearly befitting as most of the architecture – forts, palaces, temples, havelis and even houses are built in vivid shades of blue.

JD2.claim: Jodhpur dates to 1459 and was founded by Rao Jodha, chief of the Rathore clan.

evidence.quote: Jodhpur marks its origin back to the year of 1459 AD.
Rao Jodha, the chief of Rathore Clan is credited with the origin of Jodhpur in India.

JD3.claim: Jodhpur's airport is about 5 km from the centre, with flights to Delhi and Mumbai; direct trains run from all the metros.

evidence.quote: Jodhpur is connected to Delhi and Mumbai and the airport is about 5 kilometres from the city centre.
Jodhpur is well-connected by direct trains from all metros and major cities in India

JD4.claim: The two-day Marwar Festival, Jodhpur's best known, is held in Ashwin (September–October).

evidence.quote: The most popular festival in Jodhpur is the Marwar Festival. The two-day festival is held every year in the month of Ashwin (between September and October) in memory of the heroes of Rajasthan.

JD5.claim: Mandore, the ancient capital of Marwar north of the city, has temple-style cenotaphs of Jodhpur's rulers.

evidence.quote: Towards the north of Jodhpur city is the ancient capital of
Jodhpur’s former rulers.

JDM1.claim: Mehrangarh rises from a hill 125 metres above Jodhpur and still shows cannonball marks on its second gate.

evidence.quote: Rising perpendicular and impregnable from a hill which is 125 metres above Jodhpur’s skyline is the Mehrangarh Fort.
Mehrangarh Fort still bears the imprints of cannonball attacks courtesy the armies of Jaipur on its second gate.

JDM2.claim: Inside are the Moti Mahal (Pearl Hall), the mirrored Sheesh Mahal and the lavish Phool Mahal.

evidence.quote: Moti Mahal, as the name suggests, is the Pearl Hall where the royal families held their audience.
This magnificent piece of architecture is adorned with walls of mirror work that stretch across ceilings and to the floors.
Going by the name, the Phool Mahal or Flower Hall is the most exorbitant of all the halls in the palace.

JDM3.claim: The fort was first built around 1459 by Rao Jodha; most of what stands is 17th-century, and it has seven gates including Jai Pol.

evidence.quote: It was initially built around 1459 by the Rajput ruler of Rathore clan Rao Jodha
though most of the existing structure is from the 17th century built by his successors
The fort has seven gates, including the main entrance, Jai Pol (meaning 'victory gate')

JDM4.claim: The Chamunda Mataji temple in the fort honours Rao Jodha's favourite goddess.

evidence.quote: Chamunda Mataji was Rao Jodha’s favourite goddess and so her idol was bought to the Mehrangarh Fort.

JDJ1.claim: Jaswant Thada is a milky-white 19th-century memorial to Jaswant Singh, run by the Mehrangarh Museum Trust, with a portrait museum.

evidence.quote: This milky white memorial built towards the end of the 19th century as a tribute to the leader Jaswant Singh is a huge tourist attraction.
Jaswant Thada is managed and looked after by the Mehrangarh Museum Trust (MMT) and is open to public.

JDU1.claim: Umaid Bhawan Palace was begun in 1929 by Maharaja Umaid Singh, designed by H. V. Lanchester, and is one of the world's largest private homes.

evidence.quote: Umaid Bhawan Palace was built by Maharaja Umaid Singh in 1929 to counter a famine which had hit the state at the time.
The palace was designed by HV Lanchester, a renowned British architect, and was completed in 16 years.
It is recognised as one of the largest private homes in the world and also one of the more spectacular buildings.

JDG1.claim: Ghanta Ghar, the clock tower built by Maharaja Sardar Singh, stands in Sardar Market, known for spices, clothes and jewellery.

evidence.quote: Ghanta Ghar, also known as the clock tower, is situated in
among tourists for spices, traditional clothes and fancy

JS1.claim: Jaisalmer, the 'Golden City', sits near the Pakistan border on the edge of the Thar Desert; its landmark is the Sonar Qila.

evidence.quote: This 'Golden City’ is located close to the Pakistan border and in close proximity to the Thar Desert.
The city’s most prominent landmark is the Jaisalmer Fort, also called Sonar Qila (Golden Fort).

JS2.claim: Rawal Jaisal built a mud fort here in 1156 and named his capital Jaisalmer.

evidence.quote: It was in 1156 that Rawal Jaisal constructed a mud fort, named it Jaisalmer after himself and declared it his capital.

JS3.claim: The Desert Festival, with camel races, camel polo and folk dances, is held around January–February.

evidence.quote: Organised by the Department of Tourism around January-February, the Desert Festival is the best place to enjoy rich and colourful Rajasthani folk culture.
The high points of the festival are puppeteers, acrobats, camel races, camel polo, folk dances, etc.

JS4.claim: Jaisalmer has an airport with flights from Jaipur, Delhi, Mumbai, Bengaluru and Surat, direct trains from Delhi, and buses from Jodhpur, Bikaner and Jaipur.

evidence.quote: Jaisalmer has the civil airport facility and has direct air connectivity from Jaipur, delhi, mumbai, Banglore and surat in jaislmer.
Jaisalmer is connected to Jodhpur, Bikaner and Jaipur by bus and taxi.
There is a direct train service between Jaisalmer and Delhi, with a few trains connecting the two cities.

JS5.claim: October to March is the season for desert camping, at Sam among other places.

evidence.quote: For the adventurous folk, the ideal time to head out for camping would be between October to March.

JSF1.claim: Jaisalmer Fort is a World Heritage Site and still a living fort, with shops, hotels and old havelis where families live.

evidence.quote: Unlike most other forts in India, Jaisalmer Fort is not just a tourist attraction.
It houses shops, hotels and ancient havelis (homes) where generations continue to live.
This fort is a world heritage site and forms an important plot point in one of Satyajit Ray’s famous Feluda stories and corresponding movie, Sonar Kela (The Golden Fortress).

JSF2.claim: The fort's 12th- and 15th-century Jain temples are carved from yellow sandstone in the Dilwara style.

evidence.quote: The Jain Temples located inside the Jaisalmer Fort date back to the 12th and 15th centuries.
They have been built in the famed Dilwara style which is known for its beautiful architecture.

JSP1.claim: Patwon ki Haveli is among Jaisalmer's largest and most elaborately carved havelis: five storeys on a narrow street.

evidence.quote: Among the largest and the most elaborately carved havelis in Jaisalmer, this five-storey structure sits proudly in a narrow street.

JSG1.claim: At Gadisar Lake, a laser and water-screen show tells the story of Jaisalmer and its fort.

evidence.quote: Laser Water Show at Gadisar Lake is one of the first and largest Laser Water Show having water screen projection mapping using 3-chip DLP projectors of 25,000 lumens.

JSS1.claim: Camel and camel-cart safaris are offered at the Sam and Khuri sand dunes.

evidence.quote: Tourists can enjoy camel/camel cart safari at Sam sand dunes as well as at Khuri sand dunes.

JSS2.claim: Jeep safaris and dune bashing run at Lakhmana and other dune tracks near Sam and Khuri.

evidence.quote: tourists can enjoy jeep safari/ dunes bashing at Lakhmna sand dunes as well as at some other isolated sand dune tracks near Sam and Khuri.

JSK1.claim: Kuldhara, about 18 km from Jaisalmer, is a village abandoned by its people in the 1800s.

evidence.quote: Located about 18 km from the city of Jaisalmer is this old town that was abandoned by its villagers in the 1800s.

JSB1.claim: Bada Bagh, about 6 km north, holds the royal cenotaphs of Jaisalmer and is good at sunset.

evidence.quote: About 6 kilometres to the north of Jaisalmer lies Bada Bagh, also called Barabagh (literally Big Garden).
The location of the garden is such that it offers wonderful sunset vistas to tourists.

PK1.claim: Pushkar, one of India's oldest towns, lies north-west of Ajmer, surrounded by hills on three sides.

evidence.quote: Pushkar is one of the oldest cities in India.
Pushkar is surrounded by hillocks on three sides.

PK2.claim: Pushkar has the only temple dedicated to Lord Brahma in the world.

evidence.quote: The city of Pushkar is home to the only temple dedicated to Lord Brahma in the whole world.

PK3.claim: As a temple town, Pushkar serves only vegetarian food; try kachori, malpua and lassi.

evidence.quote: Being a temple town, Pushkar exclusively offers vegetarian food, but the sheer variety of the food makes the trip completely worth it.

PK4.claim: Pushkar's station is linked to Ajmer station, 14 km away; buses run to Jaipur and Jodhpur from the Ajmer bus stand.

evidence.quote: Pushkar Terminus Railway station which is operational since 2012, is connected to Ajmer railway station located at a distance of 14 kilometres.
Regular buses ply from Pushkar to the major cities of Jaipur, Jodhpur and Ajmer from the Ajmer bus stand.

PK5.claim: Sadar Bazar is Pushkar's main shopping street, for silver jewellery, embroidered clothes and leather goods.

evidence.quote: The main shopping area is the Sadar Bazar.
offer items like silver jewellery, accessories, embroidered clothes, leather goods, and decorative items

PKL1.claim: Pushkar Lake, 'Tirtha Raj', is ringed by 52 bathing ghats and over 400 temples.

evidence.quote: According to Hindu scriptures, the sacred Pushkar Lake is described as ‘Tirtha Raj’, the king of all pilgrimage sites.
Pushkar Lake is surrounded by 52 bathing ghats and over 400 temples

PKB1.claim: The marble Brahma temple has a red spire, a swan emblem and a four-faced idol of Brahma.

evidence.quote: Built with marble and decorated with silver coins, this temple can be identified by its red spire and the image of a swan (considered sacred to Lord Brahma).
The chaturmukhi (four faced) idol of Lord Brahma is housed in the inner sanctum.

PKS1.claim: The Savitri Mata temple sits on a hill behind the Brahma temple; a ropeway opened in 2016 gives views of the whole town.

evidence.quote: Dedicated to Lord Brahma's first wife, Goddess Savitri, this temple is situated on a hillock right behind the Brahma temple.
Overlooking the beautiful and scenic Pushkar Lake, the Savitri Mata Ropeway gives a bird’s eye view of the entire town of Pushkar.
The Savitri Mata ropeway was inaugurated in the year 2016.

PKF1.claim: The Pushkar Fair is a week-long camel and livestock fair held between October and November, one of the world's largest.

evidence.quote: is an annual weeklong camel and livestock fair held in the town of Pushkar between the months of October and November
It is one of the world's largest camel

PKF2.claim: Fair competitions include 'matka phod', 'longest moustache' and a bridal contest.

evidence.quote: Competitions such as the ‘matka phod’, ‘longest moustache’ and ‘bridal competition’

PKF3.claim: The best camping season in Pushkar is October to February; camps sit near the fairground.

evidence.quote: Some of the most preferred campsites in Pushkar are located near the Pushkar fair grounds, at the edge of the Desert.
The best time for camping in Pushkar is from October to February

AJ1.claim: Ajmer is a pilgrimage centre for Hindus and Muslims; the dargah of Khwaja Moinuddin Chishti draws Muslims from around the world.

evidence.quote: Ajmer remains a popular tourist attraction, in addition to being a pilgrimage centre for both Hindus and Muslims.
The final resting place of the Sufi Saint, Khwaja Moinuddin Hasan Chisti, is visited by Muslims from all over the world

AJ2.claim: Ajmer was founded by Raja Ajaypal Chauhan in the 7th century and was the Chauhan capital until the 12th century.

evidence.quote: The city was founded by Raja Ajaypal Chauhan in the 7th century AD and the city remained as the epicentre of the Chauhan Dynasty till the 12th century AD.

AJ3.claim: Kishangarh Airport is about 30 km away; Ajmer is on the Delhi–Jaipur–Ahmedabad–Mumbai railway line.

evidence.quote: The nearest airport is Kishangarh Airport, which is about 30 kilometres away and helps Ajmer remain well-connected with major Indian cities.
Ajmer is located on the Delhi-Jaipur-Marwar-Ahmedabad-Mumbai railway line.

AJ4.claim: The Adhai Din Ka Jhonpra began as a Sanskrit college and was turned into a mosque in 1198.

evidence.quote: The Adhai Din Ka Jhonpda was originally built to function as a Sanskrit college but was later converted into a mosque by Sultan Ghori in 1198 AD.

AJD1.claim: The dargah of Mu'in al-Din Chishti is a Sufi shrine complex that can draw up to 20,000 pilgrims a day, and hundreds of thousands at the Urs.

evidence.quote: is a Sufi dargah complex incorporating the shrine of Mu'in al-Din Chishti , several tombs, and a mosque
that can attract up to 20,000 pilgrims per day, swelling to hundred of thousands on Chishti's urs

AJD2.claim: The dargah is revered by Hindus and Muslims alike.

evidence.quote: the Dargah is revered equally by both Hindus and Muslims

AJA1.claim: Ana Sagar was built between 1135 and 1150; Jahangir added the Daulat Bagh gardens and Shah Jahan five marble pavilions (the Baradari).

evidence.quote: Anasagar Lake is a scenic artificial lake, commissioned and built by Arnoraj Chauhan, son of Ajaypal Chauhan, between 1135 and 1150 AD.
Mughal Emperor Jahangir added his touch to the lake by laying out the Daulat Bagh Gardens near the lake.
Emperor Shah Jahan too, contributed to the expansion by building five pavilions, known as the Baradari

RB1.claim: Ranthambore National Park, 14 km from Sawai Madhopur, covers 392 sq km between the Aravallis and Vindhyas and is home to tigers and over 300 bird species.

evidence.quote: Situated 14 km from Sawai Madhopur, the Ranthambore Park gets its name from the Ranthambore Fort situated within its boundaries.
The National Park, situated amidst the Aravalis and Vindhya ranges is spreads over an area of 392 sq.km of thick forest punctuated with pleasant waterfalls.
It is home to the elusive tiger, other animals found here include chinkara, sambhar, cheetal and over 300 species of birds.

RB2.claim: A safari is the best way to see Ranthambore's tigers, sloth bears and leopards; book on the Rajasthan wildlife website.

evidence.quote: One of the best ways to observe wildlife at the Ranthambore National Park is through a safari.
Apart from the royal Bengal tiger, you can also spot sloth bears, leopards, jackals, foxes and hyenas.
For information & online reservations, visit: http://www.rajasthanwildlife.rajasthan.gov.in/bookTrip.do

RB3.claim: Sawai Madhopur has regular trains; Jaipur airport, 150–170 km away, is the closest.

evidence.quote: You can easily get regular trains to Sawai Madhopur from other major cities of the country.
The Jaipur Airport is the closest and is located 150-170 kilometres away.

RBF1.claim: Ranthambore Fort was built by the Chauhans in the 10th century; it has temples, tanks, great gates and walls.

evidence.quote: The noteworthy Ranthambore Fort was built by the Chauhan rulers in the 10th century.
The fort is characterised by temples, tanks, massive gates and huge walls.

RBF2.claim: The Trinetra Ganesh temple inside the fort holds a fair on Bhadrapad Chaturthi.

evidence.quote: Every year a fair is held on Chaturthi of Bhadrapad month.

MA1.claim: Mount Abu is Rajasthan's only hill station, at 1,722 metres in the Aravallis.

evidence.quote: Mount Abu, the state’s only hill station stands at a height of 1722 metres above sea level, and is embraced by lush green hills of the Aravalli range.

MA2.claim: The nearest railway station is 28 km away on the Delhi–Mumbai line; Udaipur airport is 176 km away.

evidence.quote: The railway station at Mount Abu is located at a distance of 28 kilometres from the city.
This railway station lies on the connecting rail line between Delhi and Mumbai.
the closest airport is the Maharana Pratap Airport in Dabok, Udaipur, located at a distance of 176 kilometres from Mount Abu

MA3.claim: Mount Abu holds a summer festival from Buddha Purnima and a winter festival in December.

evidence.quote: Starting on the day of Buddha Poornima, the summer festival celebrates the vibrancy of Rajasthani culture
The annual Winter Festival held at Mount Abu in December pays homage to the rich culture and tradition of Rajasthan.

MA4.claim: The 288 sq km Mount Abu Wildlife Sanctuary is home to leopards, striped hyenas and grey jungle fowl.

evidence.quote: Covering 288 square kilometres of area, the Mount Abu Wildlife Sanctuary is a part of the subtropical forest in this region.
including the Indian fox, pangolin, grey jungle fowl, striped hyena, and also Indian leopard, the apex predator here

MAD1.claim: The five white-marble Dilwara Jain temples, built between the 11th and 13th centuries, are about 2.5 km from Mount Abu.

evidence.quote: Established some time in between the 11th and 13th centuries, the Dilwara Jain temples are considered to be among the best specimens of architectural perfection in the country.
A complex of five temple structures, the Dilwara Jain temples are located at a distance of about 2.5 kilometres from Mount Abu.

MAD2.claim: Dilwara is famous for its pure white marble and intricate carving.

evidence.quote: famous for their use of a very pure white marble and intricate marble carvings

MAN1.claim: Nakki Lake is known for sunset boat rides, the immersion of Mahatma Gandhi's ashes and nearby Toad Rock.

evidence.quote: You can choose to take a boat ride at the lake and watch the sun set past the beautiful hills surrounding this place.
Nakki Lake is also popular for being the place where the ashes of Mahatma Gandhi had been immersed.
Toad rock, a place for sightseeing in Mount Abu is located close to Nakki Lake.

MAG1.claim: Guru Shikhar is the highest point of the range; about 300 steps lead to the temple of Guru Dattatreya.

evidence.quote: Recognized as the highest point on this mountain range, Guru Shikhar is an exquisite place for sightseeing in Mount Abu.
Taking about 300 steps up to Guru Shikhar, you reach the temple of Guru Dattatreya

CH1.claim: Chittorgarh Fort stands on a 180-metre hill and covers 700 acres.

evidence.quote: Chittorgarh is named after its most imposing structure, the Chittorgarh Fort which stands atop a 180 metre high hill and is spread across 700 acres.

overview.text:
Udaipur, often called the 'Venice of the East', is built around lakes and ringed by the green hills of the Aravallis. Maharana Udai Singh II founded it in 1553 as the new capital of Mewar.

The City Palace towers over Lake Pichola, where the Lake Palace and Jag Mandir sit on islands; to the north, Fateh Sagar has its own islands and India's only island solar observatory. Old lanes run down from the Jagdish Temple to the ghats, and in the evening Bagore-ki-Haveli stages a show of Rajasthani folk dance.

Most visitors spend two or three days, with a sunset boat ride on Pichola as the highlight.

overview.text:
The City Palace towers over Lake Pichola on a hill ringed with crenellated walls — a maze of courtyards, pavilions, terraces, corridors and hanging gardens. You enter through the Tripolia, a triple-arched gate with eight marble porticos.

Inside, look for the Mor Chowk with its glass peacock mosaics and the Chini Chitrashala's blue-and-white tiles. The Crystal Gallery holds one of the largest collections of Osler cut glass anywhere, most of it ordered by Maharana Sajjan Singh in 1878. In the evening, a sound and light show at Manak Chowk tells the story of Mewar.

overview.text:
Jodhpur, Rajasthan's second-largest city, is known as the Blue City because so many of its forts, temples, havelis and houses are painted in vivid shades of blue. It dates to 1459, when Rao Jodha, chief of the Rathore clan, founded it.

Mehrangarh Fort looms from a rocky ridge above the old city; below it are the white marble Jaswant Thada, the busy clock-tower market and, across town, the vast Umaid Bhawan Palace. North of the city, Mandore — Marwar's ancient capital — has the cenotaphs of Jodhpur's rulers.

images.alt: Mehrangarh Fort's walls rising sheer above Jodhpur
images.caption: Mehrangarh Fort, Jodhpur

overview.text:
Mehrangarh rises sheer from a hill 125 metres above Jodhpur's skyline. Rao Jodha first built it around 1459, though most of what stands today is 17th-century work by his successors. It has seven gates, including the main Jai Pol, and its second gate still bears the marks of cannonballs fired by the armies of Jaipur.

Inside are the Moti Mahal, the Pearl Hall where the royal family held audience; the Sheesh Mahal, covered in mirror work from floor to ceiling; and the lavish Phool Mahal. The Chamunda Mataji temple honours Rao Jodha's favourite goddess.

overview.text:
Jaisalmer, the 'Golden City', lies close to the Pakistan border on the edge of the Thar Desert. Rawal Jaisal built a mud fort here in 1156 and made it his capital, and the town's great landmark is still the fort — the Sonar Qila, or Golden Fort.

Unlike most forts, Jaisalmer's is lived in: shops, hotels and old havelis fill it. Below it are some of Rajasthan's most richly carved havelis, the Gadisar Lake, and the royal cenotaphs at Bada Bagh; out in the desert, camel safaris and camps run at the Sam and Khuri dunes.

overview.text:
Jaisalmer Fort, the Sonar Qila, seems to rise from the desert itself. It is a World Heritage Site, and unlike most forts in India it is not just a sight: it houses shops, hotels and old havelis where families have lived for generations.

Inside are Jain temples from the 12th and 15th centuries, carved from yellow sandstone in the famous Dilwara style. The fort also gave Satyajit Ray the setting for his Feluda story Sonar Kella.

overview.text:
Pushkar, north-west of Ajmer, is one of the oldest towns in India, surrounded by hills on three sides. Its sacred lake is ringed by 52 bathing ghats and over 400 temples, and the town has the only temple in the world dedicated to Lord Brahma.

Pushkar is a temple town, so its food is vegetarian — kachori, malpua and lassi from cafés along the ghats. Every year between October and November it hosts one of the world's largest camel and livestock fairs.

Ajmer was founded by Raja Ajaypal Chauhan in the 7th century and remained the Chauhan capital until the 12th century. Today it is a pilgrimage centre for both Hindus and Muslims: the final resting place of the Sufi saint Khwaja Moinuddin Chishti draws Muslims from all over the world.

Beyond the dargah, the city has the Ana Sagar lake with its Mughal marble pavilions and the Adhai Din Ka Jhonpra mosque. Pushkar is just 14 km away.

Ranthambore National Park lies 14 km from Sawai Madhopur, between the Aravalli and Vindhya ranges. Its 392 sq km of forest is home to the tiger, along with chinkara, sambar and chital and over 300 species of birds.

The park takes its name from Ranthambore Fort, built by the Chauhans in the 10th century and now one of the Hill Forts of Rajasthan World Heritage Site.

overview.text:
The Chauhan rulers built Ranthambore Fort in the 10th century, and its position made it ideal for keeping enemies at bay. It is linked to the story of the royal women's jauhar during Alauddin Khilji's siege of 1303. Temples, tanks, massive gates and walls fill the hilltop, which is part of the Hill Forts of Rajasthan World Heritage Site.

The Trinetra Ganesh temple inside the fort holds a fair every year on Bhadrapad Chaturthi.

Mount Abu is Rajasthan's only hill station, 1,722 metres up in the green Aravalli hills — a cool escape from the desert, and a place of great importance to Jains.

Its best-known sights are the white-marble Dilwara Jain temples, Nakki Lake with its boats and Toad Rock, and Guru Shikhar, the highest point of the range. A 288 sq km wildlife sanctuary covers the forest around it.

overview.text:
Chittorgarh Fort stands on a 180-metre hill and covers 700 acres. This Rajput stronghold was attacked three times: by Alauddin Khilji in 1303, by Bahadur Shah of Gujarat in 1533, and by the Mughal emperor Akbar, who seized it in 1568. It is one of the six Hill Forts of Rajasthan on UNESCO's World Heritage list.

Inside are the nine-storey Vijay Stambh (Tower of Victory), the 12th-century Kirti Stambh (Tower of Fame) dedicated to the first Jain Tirthankara, and the temple where Meerabai worshipped Krishna.

overview.text:
Kumbhalgarh lies in the Aravallis 84 km north of Udaipur. Its fort, built by Rana Kumbha in the 15th century, is Mewar's most important after Chittorgarh, and its wall runs for 36 km — one of the longest continuous walls in the world. Maharana Pratap was born here.

The Kumbhalgarh Wildlife Sanctuary surrounds the fort, home to leopards, sloth bears and wolves, and the state's three-day Kumbhalgarh Festival brings folk performances by day and light shows at night.

Kumbhalgarh, 84 km north of Udaipur, is the second most important citadel of Mewar after Chittorgarh. Rana Kumbha built it in the 15th century, and its remote, rugged site made it a refuge for Mewar's rulers. Its wall runs for 36 km — one of the longest continuous walls in the world — and Maharana Pratap was born here. It is one of the six Hill Forts of Rajasthan World Heritage Site.

Inside, see the Neelkanth Mahadev temple of 1458, with a six-foot stone Shivling, and the nine Golerao Jain temples.

overview.text:
Bikaner was founded in 1488 by Rao Bika, a Rathore prince and son of Jodhpur's founder. Its great sight is Junagarh, a fort that has never been captured; nearby are the National Research Centre on Camel, with camel rides and camel-milk treats, and the Karni Mata temple at Deshnok, famous for the rats that roam it.

On the second weekend of January the city celebrates its Camel Festival.

itineraries.summary: The City Palace, Jagdish Temple and a sunset boat on Lake Pichola on day one; Saheliyon-ki-Bari, Fateh Sagar, the ropeway and the Dharohar show on day two.
itineraries.seoTitle: Udaipur 2-Day Itinerary: City Palace, Pichola & More
itineraries.seoDescription: Two days in Udaipur: the City Palace, Jagdish Temple, a sunset boat ride on Lake Pichola, Saheliyon-ki-Bari, Fateh Sagar and the Bagore-ki-Haveli dance show.

plan.overview: Udaipur's main sights cluster around Lake Pichola, so the first day is on foot in the old city; the second goes north to Fateh Sagar and ends with folk dance on the ghats.
plan.start: Maharana Pratap Airport (Dabok) or Udaipur station
plan.transport: Walk in the old city; autos and cabs to Fateh Sagar and the ropeway.
plan.season: October to January is the most comfortable season.

days.title: Day 1: City Palace and Lake Pichola
days.summary:
Morning: Jagdish Temple, then the City Palace — Mor Chowk and the Crystal Gallery.

Afternoon: rest out of the sun.

Evening: a sunset boat ride on Lake Pichola past the Lake Palace and Jag Mandir.

days.title: Day 2: Fateh Sagar and the ghats
days.summary:
Morning: Saheliyon-ki-Bari, then Fateh Sagar and the Maharana Pratap statue on Moti Magri.

itineraries.title: Jaisalmer in 2 days: the fort and the dunes
itineraries.summary: The living fort, its Jain temples and the havelis on day one; Kuldhara, a camel safari at Sam and a night in a desert camp on day two.
itineraries.seoTitle: Jaisalmer 2-Day Itinerary: Fort, Havelis & Desert Camp
itineraries.seoDescription: Two days in Jaisalmer: the living Sonar Qila and Jain temples, Patwon ki Haveli, Gadisar Lake, Kuldhara, a Sam camel safari and a desert camp.

plan.overview: Jaisalmer rewards one day in town and one in the desert. See the fort early, then head out to the dunes for sunset and a night under the stars.
plan.transport: Walk in the fort and old town; a jeep or cab to Kuldhara and Sam.
plan.season: October to March is the desert season.

days.title: Day 1: The Golden Fort and havelis
days.summary:
Morning: the lanes and Jain temples of Jaisalmer Fort.

Afternoon: Patwon ki Haveli; rest in the heat of the day.

Evening: sunset at Bada Bagh, then the laser show at Gadisar Lake.

days.title: Day 2: Kuldhara and the Sam dunes
days.summary:
Afternoon: drive out to the abandoned village of Kuldhara.

Evening: a camel or jeep safari at Sam for sunset, then a night in a desert camp.

budget.assumptions: VacayOut lists only fees it could check with an official source; hotels, transport and meals are not estimated. Check current prices before you book.

booking.detail: Book ahead, especially around the Desert Festival in January–February.

alternatives: Visiting in January–February? Time your trip for the Desert Festival.
Continue to Jodhpur or Bikaner by road or train.
tips: Carry warm layers — desert nights are cold in winter.
Agree the safari route and price in advance.

itineraries.title: Jodhpur in 2 days: Mehrangarh and the Blue City
itineraries.summary: Mehrangarh Fort, Jaswant Thada and the clock-tower market on day one; Umaid Bhawan and Mandore on day two.
itineraries.seoDescription: Two days in Jodhpur: Mehrangarh Fort, Jaswant Thada, Sardar Market and the clock tower, Umaid Bhawan Palace and the Mandore cenotaphs.

plan.overview: Spend the first day in the old city under Mehrangarh, and the second on the grand 20th-century palace and the ancient capital at Mandore.
plan.transport: Autos and cabs; walk in the old city.
plan.season: October to January is the most comfortable season.

days.title: Day 1: Mehrangarh and the old city
days.summary:
Morning: Mehrangarh Fort — the gates, the Sheesh Mahal and Phool Mahal.

Afternoon: walk down to Jaswant Thada.

Evening: the market around the clock tower.

days.title: Day 2: Umaid Bhawan and Mandore
days.summary:
Morning: Umaid Bhawan Palace.

Afternoon: the cenotaphs and gardens of Mandore, Marwar's ancient capital.

budget.assumptions: VacayOut lists only fees it could check with an official source; hotels, transport and meals are not estimated. Check current prices before you book.

booking.detail: Stay in the old city for views of Mehrangarh.

alternatives: Come in September–October for the Marwar Festival.
tips: Visit Mehrangarh early, before the heat.
Wear good shoes for the fort ramps.

itineraries.title: Pushkar and Ajmer in 2 days
itineraries.summary: Ajmer's dargah and Ana Sagar on day one; Pushkar's ghats, Brahma temple and the Savitri ropeway on day two.
itineraries.seoTitle: Pushkar & Ajmer 2-Day Itinerary: Dargah, Lake & Temples
itineraries.seoDescription: Two days in Ajmer and Pushkar: the Ajmer Sharif Dargah, Ana Sagar's Baradari, Pushkar Lake's ghats, the Brahma Temple and the Savitri Mata ropeway.

plan.overview: Ajmer and Pushkar are just 14 km apart, so they pair perfectly: the Sufi shrine one day, the Hindu pilgrim town the next.
plan.transport: Cabs and buses between Ajmer and Pushkar; walk in both towns.
plan.season: October to March; the Pushkar camel fair is in October–November.

days.title: Day 1: Ajmer
days.summary:
Morning: the Ajmer Sharif Dargah (cover your head).

Afternoon: the Adhai Din Ka Jhonpra.

Evening: the marble Baradari on Ana Sagar, then on to Pushkar.
days.travel: Ajmer to Pushkar: 14 km by road.

days.title: Day 2: Pushkar
days.summary:
Morning: walk the ghats of Pushkar Lake, then the Brahma Temple.

Afternoon: the ropeway to the Savitri Mata temple; shop in Sadar Bazar.

Evening: aarti at the ghats.
days.meals: Pushkar is vegetarian — try malpua and lassi.

booking.detail: Book months ahead if your dates fall during the camel fair.

Continue to Jaipur or Jodhpur by bus from Ajmer.
tips: Dress modestly at both the dargah and the ghats.

itineraries.title: Ranthambore in 2 days: safaris and the fort
itineraries.summary: Two park safaris for the best chance of a tiger, and a morning at Ranthambore Fort and its Ganesh temple.
itineraries.seoDescription: Two days in Ranthambore: two safaris in the national park, Ranthambore Fort and the Trinetra Ganesh temple, and how to book.

plan.overview: Plan two safaris — one each day — and fit Ranthambore Fort between them. Sawai Madhopur is the base.
plan.transport: Safari vehicles inside the park; cabs to the fort.
plan.season: October to January is the most comfortable season.

days.title: Day 1: Arrive and first safari
days.summary:
Arrive in Sawai Madhopur.

Afternoon: your first safari in the national park.

days.title: Day 2: Safari and fort
days.summary:

itineraries.title: Mewar in 4 days: Udaipur, Kumbhalgarh and Chittorgarh
itineraries.summary: Two days in Udaipur, a day at Kumbhalgarh's great wall and a day at Chittorgarh's fort — the heart of Mewar.

itineraries.seoDescription: Four days in Mewar: Udaipur's City Palace and lakes, the 36 km wall of Kumbhalgarh and Chittorgarh's 700-acre fort with Vijay Stambh.

plan.overview: Base yourself in Udaipur and add two of the Hill Forts of Rajasthan: Kumbhalgarh to the north and Chittorgarh to the east.
plan.transport: A hired car is easiest for Kumbhalgarh and Chittorgarh.
plan.season: October to January; Kumbhalgarh is also pleasant in summer.

days.title: Day 1: Udaipur's City Palace and Pichola

days.title: Day 2: Fateh Sagar and Bagore-ki-Haveli

days.title: Day 3: Kumbhalgarh

days.title: Day 4: Chittorgarh

Add Ranthambore, another Hill Fort, further east.
tips: Wear good shoes for the ramparts.

itineraries.title: Rajasthan in 10 days: Jaipur, Pushkar, Jodhpur, Jaisalmer and Udaipur
itineraries.summary: The classic loop: Jaipur's forts, holy Pushkar, Jodhpur's Blue City, a night in the Thar at Jaisalmer, and the lakes of Udaipur.
itineraries.seoDescription: A 10-day Rajasthan itinerary: Jaipur, Ajmer and Pushkar, Jodhpur's Mehrangarh, Jaisalmer's fort and dunes, and Udaipur's palaces and lakes.

plan.overview: This loop links Rajasthan's best-known cities in a sensible order, finishing in Udaipur, which has its own airport. Distances are long — use trains and a driver, and keep a rest afternoon in each city.

plan.season: October to March; avoid the summer heat.

guides.title: Best time to visit Rajasthan: seasons and festivals
guides.summary: Winter, summer and monsoon in Rajasthan — what each season is like, where to go, and the festivals worth planning around.
guides.seoTitle: Best Time to Visit Rajasthan: Seasons & Festivals
guides.seoDescription: When to visit Rajasthan: mild winters from October, 48°C summers, the green monsoon, and festivals from the Pushkar Fair to the Desert Festival.

body.intro: Rajasthan has three seasons, and the right one depends on what you want to do. Here's how to choose.

sections.heading: Winter (about October to January)
sections.text: The best season for most trips. Days are mild — roughly 10–30°C across most of the state — and sunny, though nights get chilly. It's also festival season: the Jaipur Literature Festival, the Udaipur World Music Festival and the Pushkar Fair all fall in winter.

sections.heading: Summer
sections.text: Hot and dry, with temperatures up to 48°C — hardest around the Thar Desert. If you travel now, head for Mount Abu, Ranakpur and Kumbhalgarh, which stay pleasant.

sections.heading: Monsoon
sections.text: The rains turn the landscape green, and towns prepare for the Teej festival.

items.title: Pushkar Camel Fair
items.body: A week between October and November.

items.title: Bikaner Camel Festival
items.body: The second Saturday and Sunday of January.

items.title: Desert Festival, Jaisalmer
items.body: Around January–February.

items.title: Marwar Festival, Jodhpur
items.body: Two days in Ashwin (September–October).

checklist: Pack light cotton for summer and layers for winter nights

guides.title: How to reach and get around Rajasthan
guides.summary: The airports, rail hubs and highways that connect Rajasthan's cities — and the nearest airport for each destination.
guides.seoTitle: How to Reach Rajasthan: Airports, Trains & Roads
guides.seoDescription: Getting to and around Rajasthan: Jaipur, Jodhpur and Udaipur airports, rail hubs at Jaipur and Kota, NH-8, and the nearest airport for each city.

body.intro: Rajasthan is big and its cities are far apart. Fly into the airport nearest your first stop, and use trains and roads between cities.

items.title: Jaipur
items.body: The state's international airport (Sanganer).

items.title: Jodhpur
items.body: Domestic; about 5 km from the city.

items.title: Udaipur
items.body: Maharana Pratap Airport at Dabok, about 25 km from the city.

items.title: Jaisalmer
items.body: Direct flights from Jaipur, Delhi, Mumbai, Bengaluru and Surat.

items.title: Ajmer and Pushkar
items.body: Kishangarh Airport, about 30 km from Ajmer.

items.title: Bikaner
items.body: Nal airport, 10 km from the city.

sections.heading: Trains
sections.text: Jaipur and Kota are the main rail hubs; Udaipur, Jodhpur, Ajmer, Bikaner and Abu Road are other major stations. Pushkar's station links to Ajmer, 14 km away.

sections.heading: Roads and buses
sections.text: NH-8 between Delhi and Mumbai runs through Jaipur, Ajmer, Udaipur and Chittorgarh. The Rajasthan State Road Transport Corporation runs buses between cities.

sections.heading: Nearest airports for smaller places
sections.text: Ranthambore: Jaipur, 150–170 km. Mount Abu: Udaipur, 176 km (the nearest station is 28 km away). Chittorgarh: Udaipur, about 90 km. Kumbhalgarh: Udaipur, 98 km.

checklist: Fly into the airport nearest your first city
Book long train legs early in winter

guides.title: Ranthambore safari guide: booking, wildlife and tips
guides.summary: How to book a Ranthambore safari, what you might see, how to get there and how to give yourself the best chance of a tiger.
guides.seoTitle: Ranthambore Safari Guide: Booking & Tiger Tips
guides.seoDescription: Plan a Ranthambore safari: book on the Rajasthan wildlife website, tigers, leopards and sloth bears, getting to Sawai Madhopur and the fort.

body.intro: Ranthambore is one of India's best places to see a wild tiger. Here's how to plan your safari.

sections.heading: The park
sections.text: Ranthambore National Park lies 14 km from Sawai Madhopur, between the Aravallis and Vindhyas. Its 392 sq km of forest holds tigers, chinkara, sambar and chital, and over 300 species of birds.

sections.heading: Booking
sections.text: Information and online reservations are on the Rajasthan wildlife department's official website. Book well ahead.

sections.heading: What you might see
sections.text: Besides tigers: sloth bears, leopards, jackals, foxes and hyenas.

sections.heading: Getting there
sections.text: Regular trains run to Sawai Madhopur; Jaipur airport is the closest, 150–170 km away.

sections.heading: Ranthambore Fort
sections.text: The 10th-century Chauhan fort inside the park is part of the Hill Forts of Rajasthan World Heritage Site. Its Trinetra Ganesh temple holds a fair on Bhadrapad Chaturthi.

checklist: Carry warm layers for winter mornings

guides.title: Pushkar Camel Fair guide: when it is and how to plan
guides.summary: When the Pushkar Fair happens, what goes on, where to stay and how to combine it with Ajmer.
guides.seoTitle: Pushkar Camel Fair Guide: Dates, Camps & Tips
guides.seoDescription: Plan the Pushkar Camel Fair: held between October and November, livestock trading and competitions, camps near the fairground and tips.

body.intro: The Pushkar Fair turns a small temple town into one of the world's largest camel and livestock fairs. Plan early.

sections.heading: When
sections.text: The fair is held for about a week between October and November.

sections.heading: What happens
sections.text: Camels and livestock are traded, and competitions such as 'matka phod', the longest moustache and a bridal contest draw crowds.

sections.heading: Where to stay
sections.text: Campsites go up near the fairground at the edge of the desert; October to February is the best camping season. Book months ahead.

sections.heading: The town
sections.text: Walk the 52 ghats of Pushkar Lake and visit the Brahma Temple. Pushkar is vegetarian.

sections.heading: Getting there
sections.text: Via Ajmer: Pushkar's station is linked to Ajmer station, 14 km away; Kishangarh is the nearest airport.

guides.title: Jaisalmer desert guide: camel safaris and camps
guides.summary: Where to ride, when to go, and what to expect from a night in a Thar desert camp near Jaisalmer.
guides.seoTitle: Jaisalmer Camel Safari & Desert Camp Guide
guides.seoDescription: Plan a Jaisalmer desert trip: camel and jeep safaris at Sam and Khuri, desert camps from October to March, and the Desert Festival.

body.intro: For many travellers, a night in the Thar is the highlight of Rajasthan. Here's how to plan it.

sections.heading: Where
sections.text: Camel and camel-cart safaris run at the Sam and Khuri dunes. Jeep safaris and dune bashing run at Lakhmana and other tracks near Sam and Khuri.

sections.heading: When
sections.text: October to March is the season for desert camping. The Desert Festival — camel races, camel polo and folk dance — is held around January–February.

sections.heading: Camps
sections.text: Many camps offer tents with a bedroom, a sitting area and an attached bathroom, and camel rides as part of their packages.

sections.heading: On the way
sections.text: Stop at Kuldhara, the village abandoned in the 1800s, about 18 km from Jaisalmer.

checklist: Agree safari routes and prices first

guides.title: The Hill Forts of Rajasthan: a World Heritage guide
guides.summary: The six forts on UNESCO's list — Chittorgarh, Kumbhalgarh, Ranthambore, Gagron, Amber and Jaisalmer — and how to visit them.
guides.seoTitle: Hill Forts of Rajasthan: UNESCO World Heritage Guide
guides.seoDescription: Visit the Hill Forts of Rajasthan World Heritage Site: Chittorgarh, Kumbhalgarh, Ranthambore, Jaisalmer, Amber and Gagron, with tips for each.

body.intro: Six of Rajasthan's hill forts were inscribed together as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2013. These are the ones most travellers visit.

sections.heading: The six forts
sections.text: Chittorgarh, Kumbhalgarh, Ranthambore (Sawai Madhopur), Gagron (Jhalawar), Amber (Jaipur) and Jaisalmer.

sections.heading: Chittorgarh
sections.text: 700 acres on a 180-metre hill, besieged in 1303, 1533 and 1568. See the Vijay Stambh, built 1440–1448, and stay for the light and sound show after sunset.

sections.heading: Kumbhalgarh
sections.text: Rana Kumbha's 15th-century fort 84 km north of Udaipur, with a 36 km wall and Maharana Pratap's birthplace.

sections.heading: Jaisalmer
sections.text: A living fort of golden sandstone, still home to shops, hotels and families, with 12th–15th-century Jain temples.

sections.heading: Ranthambore
sections.text: The 10th-century Chauhan fort inside Ranthambore National Park — combine it with a tiger safari.
